quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this can change based on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must swerve and brake to avoid a hazard, do them separately. Brake first and then swerve, or swerve first and then brake. Do not do both actions at the same time.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help you control a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before you enter the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Press the handle grip to lean in the right direction. Then gently increase speed through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors. Being in this position increases your chances of being seen.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to respond to hazards.
It stops you from finding an escape route.
It gives you room to maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to respond if another driver makes a mistake. This space also allows you to safely maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.question: Are helmets required?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, you should usually:

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks is to ride straight across within your lane. Changing your path angle may push you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down at the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not try to fight the handlebars.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Generally, a group should ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT give you the best helmet protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: For the best protection, your helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fit snugly all the way around your head, and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave it behind.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If chased, slow down and approach the dog. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need?
questions.correctAnswerText: The same as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need as much space to stop as other vehicles. Always keep enough distance between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, which brakes should you use?

options.text: The front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use the front and rear brakes together for normal stops. Also downshift.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, which is NOT something you should do?

options.text: Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, ride slower and allow more stopping distance due to added weight. Your passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or your waist and hips, not the back of the bike.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together when you stop.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what tire adjustment will you likely need to make?

options.text: Make no changes to tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, so you will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important for helmet protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Good appearance
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no damage. How it looks does not affect protection.

questions.question: When being passed, which part of your lane should you stay in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: A flat front tire makes your steering feel:
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering can mean your front tire is flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping in a straight line:

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: A locked rear wheel during straight-line stopping does not cause loss of control. Keep the wheel locked until you stop. The motorcycle stays under control if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your eyes level, and do not turn your shoulders. Turning your shoulders can make you steer off course.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride in which part of your lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left part of your lane.
